long_biography.plain_text:
An early career in asset management led Hervé Barthélemy Georges Vinciguerra to create Sophis in 1985. The company built portfolio and risk-management software for banks, asset managers and hedge funds. Vinciguerra sold a majority stake to Advent International, retained a significant interest and stepped back from executive management. Misys's acquisition in 2010 completed the corporate exit. Its headline price included Sophis equity and net debt; it was not Vinciguerra's personal proceeds.

After Sophis, Vinciguerra organised investing through Alix holding companies and a family office. He is the sole beneficiary of the structure behind Alix AM, whose purpose included holding financial assets and growth-company stakes. He also invested in property, start-ups, Riskdata and Château d'Esclans; the wine interest was later sold to Moët Hennessy. Values belonging to holding companies, portfolio businesses or individual transactions remain distinct from his personal net worth. His active directorships now include property-holding and investment vehicles in France and the United Kingdom.
